name: Rockland to Carver's Harbor
note: Threads the ledges around Old Harbor, The Reach, and Green Island Knob into Carver's Harbor on Vinalhaven. Verified live 2026-09-12 as a hand-built route after direct AutoRoute fell back to a straight line on this corridor — kept here as both a sample route and a regression check for the router.

name: Rockland to Warren Island
note: Runs up West Penobscot Bay past Camden and Lincolnville, then curves around Warren Island's north end into the state park's mooring field. Verified live 2026-09-17 — AutoRoute threads this corridor cleanly; kept here as both a sample route and a regression check for the router.

name: Rockland to Perry Creek
note: Runs up West Penobscot Bay past Camden and Islesboro to the free moorings off Perry Creek's mouth on Vinalhaven/North Haven's Fox Island Thorofare side. Verified live 2026-09-18 — AutoRoute threads this corridor cleanly; kept here as both a sample route and a regression check for the router.

name: Rockland to Stonington (overnight at Perry Creek)
note: Two-leg passage: Rockland to the Perry Creek moorings (overnight stop, tagged on that waypoint), then on through the Deer Isle Thorofare approach to Stonington. Both legs verified live 2026-09-18 — AutoRoute threads each cleanly; kept here as both a sample route and a regression check for the router.

name: Rockland to WoodenBoat School
note: Long-range passage (~24nm) up through Eggemoggin Reach and the Deer Isle Thorofare archipelago to the WoodenBoat School's moorings in Center Harbor, Brooklin. Verified live 2026-09-18 after fixing a real router bug (a long-range transit bracket's clamped boundary could land on land itself, near the town of Deer Isle, with no nearby-water recovery) — kept here as both a sample route and a regression check for the router.

name: Rockland to Hadlock Cove (3 nights)
note: Four-day, three-overnight passage: Rockland to Perry Creek, to a Crotch Island-area anchorage off Stonington (user-placed, replacing the harbor itself), to Burnt Coat Harbor (Swans Island), then west of Placentia Island via Western Way into Hadlock Cove. Days 1-2 reuse the verified Rockland-Stonington-approach path; the second overnight was relocated 2026-09-24 after the harbor-side approach threaded a dangerous reroute through a real rock field off Crotch Island (15 charted underwater rocks + 1 obstruction within 100 yds, found live via the app's own hazard check) — the new anchorage point and both its approach/departure legs were re-verified live with zero hard or soft hazard flags, a cleaner result than the original. The Burnt Coat-Hadlock legs were verified live 2026-09-22 (Router.autoRouteProg + classifyFallbackSeg on every sub-leg, none a silent land/hazard fallback). 2026-09-23: a user-reported land crossing on the Swans Island headland (near Atlantic/Fir Point, NE shore) was found real and fixed by rerouting two waypoints around it; a full land-crossing sweep of the whole route also flagged the Burnt Coat Harbor loop, where a waypoint sat exactly on Burnt Coat Harbor Lighthouse's charted rock — removed (the flanking waypoints already connect cleanly without it, verified against raw NOAA ENC source data, not just the app's derived land layer). The same sweep flagged 5 segments on the decades-old Rockland-Perry Creek leg (Vinalhaven's north shore); those were confirmed as a data-pipeline artifact, not real hazards — extract_land.py's chart-priority dedup let a coarse-scale (US2) whole-island outline stand in for a real, navigable notch that the actual harbor-scale (US5) chart shows clearly as open water — and were left unchanged. A follow-up full hazard sweep (run with the app's active-region bug fixed — see below) found the 2026-09-24 SP008 approach/departure legs were never actually re-verified against real data and in fact ran straight through a genuine 19-rock field off Crotch Island, the same danger originally reported. Rebuilt both legs 2026-09-23 by following the real charted/buoyed approach (Field Ledge, Crotch Island, Moose Island Rock, and Peggy's Island Ledge buoys) then threading the Merchant Row-area ledge field beyond via a computed visibility path (grid/A* search over the raw charted rock positions, simplified and re-verified segment-by-segment), keeping SP008 as the overnight. Independently cross-checked against raw NOAA ENC UWTROC/OBSTRN data, not just the app's derived hazard layer: minimum clearance 0.051nm, just outside the app's 0.05nm hard-hazard corridor. Zero hard hazards across the full route after this fix (20 soft/shallow advisories remain, all pre-existing and expected in this area). Separately, the app's own hazard/land checker was found to silently check against whichever chart region happened to be active in a browser's localStorage rather than the route's actual area — it had been returning false '0 hazards' results for this exact route for two verification passes in a row before being caught.
